title: Superexchange coupling between a dilute Gd3+ probe and orphan spins in a valence-bond glass
authors: Patrick Colgan, Artur Solodovnyk, Jeremy P. Carlo, Scott Dietrich
abstract: The valence-bond-glass state of the 4d^1 double perovskite Ba2YMoO6 combines Mo^5+ singlets with residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins whose coupling is hard to reach with bulk probes. We probe them by electron paramagnetic resonance of a dilute Gd^3+ ion on the Y^3+ site via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K. The isostructural nonmagnetic niobate Ba2YNbO6, doped with the same Gd^3+ probe, is a fixed-lattice control. The Gd^3+ linewidth nearly doubles in the magnetic host. Dipolar coupling to the sparse orphans is nearly an order of magnitude too weak; the excess is instead reproduced by a transferred f-d superexchange of J ~ 0.2 K, so the width is a static measure of orphan-spin coupling. The half-field (Delta m_S = +/-2) satellite collapses in the magnetic host, a dynamical dephasing channel, while the unchanged g-factor marks a zero-mean random internal field. Together the two channels probe the coupling and dynamics of valence-bond-glass orphan spins.
summary: This work uses Electron Paramagnetic Resonance on a $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ probe to study the elusive "orphan" spins in a valence-bond-glass material. By comparing magnetic and nonmagnetic hosts, the researchers determined that the excess broadening is caused by a superexchange interaction, not simple dipolar coupling. This provides a detailed, two-pronged probe (static linewidth and dynamic satellite) into the coupling mechanisms of these disordered spins.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the coupling and dynamics of residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins within a valence-bond-glass state, which are difficult to probe using standard bulk magnetic measurements.
main_result: The excess linewidth in the $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ resonance is found to be due to a transferred $f–d$ superexchange coupling ($J \approx 0.2 	ext{ K}$), providing a static measure of the orphan-spin coupling, while the collapse of a satellite probes the dynamic dephasing.
method: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectroscopy using a dilute $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ probe ion, measured via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K, comparing magnetic and nonmagnetic host materials.
model_or_system: The system is the $4d^1$ double perovskite $	ext{Ba}_2	ext{YMoO}_6$ exhibiting a valence-bond-glass state, containing residual $	ext{Mo}^{5+}$ "orphan" spins. A nonmagnetic control, $	ext{Ba}_2	ext{YNbO}_6$, is used for comparison.
key_observables: $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ linewidth (static coupling measure), half-field ($\Delta m_S = \pm 2$) satellite (dynamic dephasing channel), and the $	ext{g}$-factor.
important_parameters: Superexchange coupling constant $J \approx 0.2 	ext{ K}$; linewidth difference between $	ext{Mo}$ and $	ext{Nb}$ hosts ($\approx 1.8$ times larger in $	ext{Mo}$).
main_assumptions: The excess linewidth is attributed to superexchange coupling rather than weak dipolar coupling, and the $	ext{g}$-factor remaining constant implies a zero-mean random internal field.
figures_summary: Figures compare the structure (XRD) and show the linewidth broadening and satellite collapse in the magnetic ($	ext{Mo}$) host versus the nonmagnetic ($	ext{Nb}$) control.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the difficulty of probing orphan spins. It uses EPR on the $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ probe to measure linewidth and satellite features. By comparing the magnetic ($	ext{Mo}$) and nonmagnetic ($	ext{Nb}$) hosts, it rules out dipolar coupling and quantifies the excess width via a transferred superexchange model, while the satellite collapse probes dynamics.
why_interesting: The use of EPR to distinguish between static (linewidth) and dynamic (satellite collapse) coupling mechanisms in a glassy magnetic system is highly relevant to understanding quantum dynamics in disordered quantum materials.

Figure 3 shows representative field-swept absorption spectra ∆|S21|(B) for the Nb and Mo hosts at three fre- quencies, together with the two-Dysonian fits. Each spec- trum is well described by a main Gd3+ resonance and a weaker half-field satellite on a smooth non-resonant back- ground, with comparable fit quality across the resolved frequency range and for both hosts. At fixed frequency the Mo-host resonance is visibly broader than that of the Nb host.
